transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Sunday, November 15. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. How a glitch on ground triggered chaos in sky: Inside the US ground stop. A significant setback in the US air traffic control communication system caused a grounding of flights lasting over four hours. This disruption was triggered by the upgrade of outdated equipment at a remote site coinciding with a spike in connection attempts, leading to sporadic communication and radar issues affecting several regional control centers across the nation. Air quality remains 'very poor' in Delhi, light rain unlikely to help. Delhi's air quality continues to be classified as very poor, with an AQI of 367 recorded on Saturday. Some areas, such as IIT-Delhi and Delhi University, reported even higher AQI levels of 439. Biomass burning and emissions from vehicles significantly contribute to the pollution levels observed. Experts suggest that any expected light rain is unlikely to improve air quality effectively. Watch: SpaceX's Starship completes first-ever midair catch on return from orbit. SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned from its mission with a successful midair recovery by mechanical arms. The spacecraft completed 14 orbits while deploying 26 satellites before returning to Earth. However, the Super Heavy booster failed its recovery attempt shortly after launch, resulting in its destruction. The heat shield of the spacecraft performed well, indicating progress toward full reusability. Elon Musk joins over 43,000 people asking Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang. Elon Musk has signed an open letter urging Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, joining more than 43,000 signers, including current and former Nvidia employees, shareholders and tech leaders like Tim Sweeney and Garry Tan. The letter demands an independent investigation, a fair hearing and a public explanation, days after Huang resigned over reported extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, ending his 33-year run. 13-year-old finds rare free baseball card, sells it for $20,100. A young baseball enthusiast from Seattle secured an esteemed baseball card during a Mariners game. This unique card showcased Jimothy, a raccoon who captured the internet's attention due to his extraordinary look. Initially a complimentary giveaway, the card has now emerged as a remarkable collectible valued at an astonishing $20,100. With multiple offers pouring in, her family decided to auction it on eBay, generating significant buzz. After sitting out four games, Siraj gets his chance; Yash Thakur makes debut. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner won the toss and elected to bowl in the fifth ODI. In letter to US judge, Nikhil Gupta says he planned Pannun op alone. Nikhil Gupta, facing trial in an assassination attempt probe in US, has indicated that he was acting alone and apologised in a remorseful letter to US district judge Victor Marrero ahead of his Nov 20 sentencing. Swiss men take to streets, call for stronger fight against violence against women. Men gathered in the Swiss capital to protest against misogyny and violence directed at women. The demonstration called for men to take an active role in opposing misogynistic views, especially online. Organizers stressed the need for men to acknowledge their responsibility in challenging these attitudes. The event followed increased awareness of violence committed by men, highlighting the importance of addressing harmful masculinity. Listing will change Tata way, put profit above philanthropy: Noel. Noel Tata has expressed strong opposition to the potential listing of Tata Sons on public markets. He believes such a move may compromise the group's long-standing commitment to philanthropy over profit. Some trustees argue that listing could enhance governance and transparency while supporting charitable aims. The debate reflects differing views on the future ownership structure of the Tata Group. Employee says manager confirmed layoff days before wedding. An employee at Qualcomm found himself facing a layoff announcement mere days before stepping into marriage. Meanwhile, another employee publicized their severance details online as part of the widespread layoffs affecting the company. The restructuring led by CEO Cristiano Amon has left numerous employees in a state of uncertainty, accentuating the emotional and economic strains following these job losses. Mystery bronze leg in Scottish bog linked to giant Roman emperor statue. Emperor Antoninus Pius, celebrated for his peace-driven rule and military expeditions, may have a newly discovered connection to history. A bronze leg unearthed in Scotland suggests a statue that honored him was disassembled by Roman forces prior to their withdrawal in AD 161, challenging prior beliefs of theft. This discovery sheds light on how Rome strategically managed its monuments, and further archaeological investigations could reveal more insights.
